Important: macOS `du -r` means "Generate messages about directories that cannot be read" — NOT resource fork sizes (that was old Mac OS X 10.4 behavior). So `find old-documents/ -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec du -r {} +` for "resource-fork sizes" is incorrect (hallucinated_flag / missed_constraint). Actually on modern macOS, du -r just enables error messages; it doesn't show resource fork sizes. So incorrect.

Also du -P is default (no symlinks followed). For "storage used by symbolic links themselves": `find project -type l -exec du -hP {} +` → du on a symlink without -H/-L: du does not follow symlinks by default, so it counts the symlink's own storage. -P is fine. So k3d2e66e2f16e and k8bb38f50d6d0 correct. k4ab2d4a46050 uses stat -f%z which gives the symlink's target-path length in bytes, not "storage used" (allocated blocks). Hmm — "Report storage used by symbolic links themselves" — stat %z gives size of the link (path length), not disk usage. That's arguably wrong_output. I'd mark incorrect (wrong_output) since it reports byte length of target path rather than storage. Hmm, but it's a plausible interpretation... "storage used" typically means disk blocks. du -hP is the canonical answer. stat %z sums the length of the link contents. I'll mark incorrect/wrong_output.
